Subject: GPU sizing for clinical NLP pipelines

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal sizing exercise and want your recommendation for a reserved pool that balances predictability and cost for our roadmap. High level:
- Current: 8 concurrent inference workers (small models, 2–4 batches each)
- Q1 target (prod): 40 concurrent workers supporting longer sequences and mix of embedding + generation
- Typical p95 latency SLO: ~120ms for generation, embeddings are less sensitive

We're most interested in: cluster sizing options, a minimum GPU floor we should reserve, and a 3-month ramp schedule you would propose tied to our deal stages. Also need a starting point for pricing scenarios.

Can you send a short worksheet or a couple of scenarios (conservative / aggressive) we can share with finance?

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure, Lacuna Therapeutics

Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU sizing for clinical NLP pipelines

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear summary. I've attached a short worksheet (lacuna_cap_plan_v1.xlsx) with three scenario sketches:
1) Baseline reserved floor (12 x A100 equivalent) + burst on demand (lowest cost but some throttling risk)
2) Performance-safe (24 x A100 equiv reserved; stable p95 and headroom for short peaks)
3) Aggressive onramp (40 x reserved phased over 12 weeks, aligns with Q1 target)

For each scenario the sheet shows expected concurrent worker capacity, estimated token/sec throughput, and a modeled per-token cost assuming your mix (60% embeddings, 40% generation).

Quick notes:
- If you want strict p95 latency SLAs during peak windows, plan for the performance-safe lane (scenario 2) as a minimum.
- Scenario 3 is recommended if you want to avoid any burst risk during model expansion (longer sequences).

I'll let Marissa add the dollars and deal-level pricing variants. Can we set up a 30-min follow up Thursday to align on the ramp triggers?

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: GPU sizing for clinical NLP pipelines — pricing & ramp

Sanjay / team —

Following Mateo's scenarios, I pulled three pricing bands and a recommended ramp tied to common deal milestones. Summary below (details in attached PDF):

- Option A — Conservative (12 reserved GPUs)
  - Minimum reserved: 12 GPUs (A100 equiv)
  - Ramp: Activate 50% at contract start, +25% at month 2, remaining at month 4
  - Net effect: low monthly commitment, higher unit cost on heavy days

- Option B — Balanced (24 reserved GPUs) — team recommendation if you need stable p95
  - Minimum reserved: 24 GPUs
  - Ramp: 25% at signing, +25% every 3 weeks until full (approx 9 weeks to full capacity)
  - Includes 10% warm-start credits and 5% discount on sustained usage

- Option C — Fast Onramp (40 reserved GPUs)
  - Minimum reserved: 40 GPUs (phased over 12 weeks)
  - Ramp: immediate 40% activation at kickoff, remainder evenly over next 11 weeks
  - Best for predictable peak SLAs and model expansions; pricing includes multi-month commit discount and prioritized warm pool allocation

Operational items / asks from Lacuna to finalize:
- Confirm which latency windows must be SLA-backed vs best-effort
- Expected weekly growth rate in concurrent workers (sample from your infra team helps our ramp cadence)
- Any compliance constraints for Private deployment (if you want VPC/on-prem options we can show separate costing)

Attachments: lacuna_pricing_scenarios.pdf (detailed numbers), link to HubSpot deal (above).

If that looks good, Mateo and I can draft a short mutual action plan with milestone-based triggers tied to billing phases — that usually helps procurement.

Thanks — happy to jump on the Thursday sync Mateo suggested.

—Marissa Cole
